The country helper feeds a switch whose CN, RU, HK, UNK, BY and IR cases fall through to the payload call; other values reach only process.exit (s1, s2, s5).
The helper requests hxxp://ipinfo[.]io/json and reads the response country field to choose the payload branch, which fits external_ip_geo (s1, s5).

The non-Linux short circuit exits before the country switch, whose accepted country cases or UNK fallback reach the payload call (s3, s5, s6). Thus Linux and either an accepted country or request failure are required, with a minimum of two conditions.

The platform exit and country switch decide whether _0x490324 is called at all; its body downloads archives, writes and extracts files, spawns the resulting executable and deletes files (f1:1, s3, s6). This fits enables.
The code invokes the payload for Linux and the accepted country or UNK results, with no analysis-environment test in these guards (s3, s5, s6). This fits activate.
The guards restrict payload execution to Linux and selected geographic results while accepting failed geolocation as UNK (s3, s5, s6). This fits targeting.

The claimed existence disjunction is insufficient for s11: each existing file can fail readFile and become null, after which filtering leaves an empty array and s8 returns before the POST (f1:1, s7, s8). The combination for exfiltration additionally requires at least one successful file read.

File existence enables each credential read, and the nonempty successful-read array enables the POST of the collected contents (s7, s8, s11). These tests enable the credential collection and exfiltration behaviour.
The file checks proceed to credential reads when the target artifacts exist, and the upload proceeds when collected results are available (s7, s8, s11). This fits activate.

The mapped paths are three cloud credential configuration files under the home directory; missing or unreadable files are filtered out and an empty collection suppresses the upload (f1:1, s7, s8). This fits data_availability.
